## Statement · **draft**
Let $G$ be a group and $S \subseteq G$. The set

$N_G(S) := \{\, g \in G : g S g^{-1} = S \,\} \le G$

is the **normalizer** of $S$ in $G$. For a subgroup $H \le G$, $N_G(H)$ is the **largest** subgroup of $G$ containing $H$ in which $H$ is normal.

If $H \le G$, then $H \trianglelefteq G \iff N_G(H) = G$; also $H \subseteq N_G(H)$ and $H \trianglelefteq N_G(H)$. Sylow counting: $n_p = [G : N_G(P)]$.
